newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada says to ease foreign bank rules.
newsitem.headline: Canada says to ease foreign bank rules.

text.p: The Canadian government announced plans on Friday to allow foreign banks to branch directly into Canada.
Separate legislation to relax foreign bank rules would be made public before the end of 1997, Doug Peters, secretary of state for financial institutions, said in a statement.
The announcement was made ahead of the government's proposed changes to financial sector legislation to be presented in parliament later today.
Foreign bankers have complained that Canada lagged behind its Group of Seven trading partners in opening its banking sector to foreign competition.

Under current rules, foreign banks are required to operate separately capitalized subsidiaries in Canada. The higher cost of operating a subsidiary, rather than a branch, has driven several foreign banks out of the country.

The number of foreign banks operating in Canada has dropped to 43 from a peak of about 60. A federal government "white paper" on financial reforms released last year introduced only minor changes to foreign bank rules.

After the report, both houses of parliament issued reports urging freer access to Canada's markets for foreign banks. Peters said branching would encourage new banks to enter the Canadian marketplace and allow existing foreign banks greater opportunity to compete.

"At the same time, prudential measures will be developed to ensure that the Canadian system remains strong," Peters said. Canada's big six domestic banks dominate regular banking, trusts and brokerages in the country. But they are being challenged by the Internet and the rise of new "virtual banks" planned by foreign banking giants.
